messages:
alex: FYI running into socket pileup when streaming responses from the .NET SDK. After a few minutes we see a bunch of TIME_WAIT sockets and throughput drops.
maya: Are you disposing HttpClient per request or using IHttpClientFactory?
alex: Using a singleton HttpClient created in a static helper (legacy). We do ResponseHeadersRead + streaming copy to disk.
samir: culprit is usually creating/disposing HttpClient frequently or not draining response stream before retry/dispose. Also Polly retries + ResponseHeadersRead can re-run request while previous stream is still being consumed.
irene: Can you share the code path for retries? Do you retry on the delegating handler or via HttpClientFactory configured Polly handler?
alex: We have a DelegatingHandler that applies a Polly RetryAsync(3) on transient network errors. It's applied as AddHttpMessageHandler on the client. We do: var resp = await client.GetAsync(url, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead); await resp.Content.CopyToAsync(fileStream);
maya: Two notes: 1) If the retry runs after headers are received but stream consumption hasn't finished, you can end up with multiple open requests. Either don't retry after ResponseHeadersRead, or buffer the body before retrying. 2) Prefer IHttpClientFactory + named clients to avoid socket exhaustion from per-request clients. :thumbsup:
samir: Example pattern that helped us:

```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("ingest")
  .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler
  {
    PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10),
    PooledConnectionIdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2),
    KeepAlivePingPolicy = HttpKeepAlivePingPolicy.Always // net7+ option
  });

// Retry policy should be applied BEFORE reading the stream body
Policy.Handle<HttpRequestException>()
  .RetryAsync(2, onRetry: (e, i) => { /* log */ });
```
irene: If you must retry after headers, buffer a small prefix (or whole body) into memory/temporal file then replay - but that defeats streaming. So choose: streaming (no mid-stream retry) or buffered + safe retries.
alex: That makes sense. We actually want streaming (files are large). Any idea how to make retries only when request hasn't started consuming the body?
samir: Use a policy that only retries on exceptions thrown by SendAsync before you call resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(). In practice, check response.IsSuccessStatusCode and only apply retry for 5xx/connection failures and not for cases where you've already started copying. Also add a cancellation/timeout so hanging streams get cancelled.
maya: Another practical fix: set SocketsHttpHandler.PooledConnectionLifetime to something sensible so long-lived DNS changes don't keep failing sockets, and tune MaxConnectionsPerServer. Also ensure Keep-Alive headers present from server.
alex: Quick question: is disposing HttpResponseMessage without reading stream enough to free connection? I've seen inconsistent behavior.
samir: You need to either fully consume the response body or call resp.Dispose() which will close underlying connection, but with pooling it may still count as in-use until GC finalizer if not handled. Best is to call resp.Content.Dispose() after cancel/read, or use using var resp = await client.GetAsync(..., HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead); then explicit await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync().CopyToAsync(...) and finally resp.Dispose().
irene: For our SDK, we've added a small helper that wraps streaming calls and disables retry policies once headers are received, and exposes a fast-fail cancellation token when CopyToAsync takes too long. That fixed >95% of socket leaks for us.

alex: Thanks — will try converting helper to use named client + policy that doesn't retry post-headers. I'll also bump PooledConnectionLifetime.
ci-bot: deploy scheduled: patch/3189 -> staging at 22:00 UTC (auto note)
maya: Ping me when you have a repro, happy to review the helper. Also add a small integration test that simulates transient network failure mid-stream.
alex: Will do. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
